resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS and the record date the station and lens to 1862; the Park Service and LighthouseFriends say the light was first shown in July 1863 because the lens arrived late. The 1862 date is the building.
The record's 1906 "Tower 2" is the 1906 rebuilding of the dwelling into a duplex, not a new tower.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: no Light-House Board reports before 1891 are in the corpus, so 1860s-1880s rest on LighthouseFriends and NPS pages. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted (facts and one short quote only); it quotes the 1902 inspector letter, the 1903 log, and the Detroit News 1931 interview second-hand. The 1887 Oak Island episode is told differently by LighthouseFriends (rescued by a passing Native American on the 16th; family arrived the 14th) and the NPS (wife organised a search): both are given. NPS spells Larsen, USLHS Larson. Active-light status differs (USLHS: not active; 1999 NPS inventory: Coast Guard maintains an automated beacon; Wikipedia says solar-powered), and the record's deactivated 1957 appears to be the removal of the light from the tower, not the end of the beacon. The 1899 Light-House Board report still lists Raspberry Island as flashing every ninety seconds (OCR, fuzzy match) against the 1894 change to every minute; not resolved, so the story gives only the 1894 report. Page 301 of the 1929 Bulletin is from the 1924-1929 index and the following page header; the 1932 item page was not determined. Roster is the USLHS list from the NARA registers; "Eino B. Hill (1935-)" has no end year. The Evening Star OCR is poor; the River Falls Journal (10 Dec 1896) prints the same dispatch with 14 and 15 miles. Possible record correction: the record gives deactivated 1957 and tower height 13.0 m; the USLHS gives 37 ft base to lantern and 77 ft focal height (23.5 m), not matched in the record. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Winfield is called keeper in the 1929 Bulletin but the USLHS roster lists him as first assistant 1923-1930 (story says so). LighthouseFriends dates the restoration 2005-2006 (reopened 2007), NPS 2005-2007 (story gives both). Bulletin 1932 item is on PDF page 28.
